spec.description: kura_egress_tree_class_sent_bytes by account and classid — kernel counter exported as a gauge, rate() × 8 — against the rate and ceiling the kernel is enforcing (_class_rate_bytes_per_second, _class_ceil_bytes_per_second, also × 8). A tenant riding its ceiling wants a larger floor; one far under its rate is reserving room it does not use. classid 1:<hex> is allocated per account by kura-controller and freed when the account's last instance goes, so the account label is what identifies the tenant over time. Node-level agent series, shown for the node(s) hosting the selected pod(s) — every class on those nodes, neighbours included, since they are what the tenant contends with.
spec.title: Class throughput (bits/s)

spec.expr: (max by (cluster, node, classid, account) ((sum by (cluster, pod, classid, account) (rate(kura_egress_tree_class_borrowed_packets{cluster=~"tuist-$env", namespace="kura"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (cluster, pod, classid, account) (rate(kura_egress_tree_class_borrowed_packets{cluster=~"tuist-$env", namespace="kura"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (cluster, pod, classid, account) (rate(kura_egress_tree_class_lended_packets{cluster=~"tuist-$env", namespace="kura"}[$__rate_interval])))) * on (cluster, pod) group_left(node) max by (cluster, pod, node) (kube_pod_info{cluster=~"tuist-$env", namespace="kura", pod=~".*egress-tree-agent.*"}))) and on (cluster, node) max by (cluster, node) (kube_pod_info{cluster=~"tuist-$env", namespace="kura", pod=~"$pod"})

spec.description: kura_egress_tree_class_borrowed_packets / (borrowed + lended) — HTB's own accounting of where a class's traffic came from: a packet sent within the class's own rate counts as lended, one it could only send by taking tokens from the root class counts as borrowed. Near 1 means the tenant spends its time above the floor it reserves and is a candidate for a larger one; near 0 means the floor covers its demand. A class with no floor runs on the 1 Mbit trickle the agent gives it, so it borrows nearly everything by construction — read this against the rate on 'Class throughput'. Node-level agent series, shown for the node(s) hosting the selected pod(s).
spec.title: Class borrow ratio

spec.expr: sum by (level) (count_over_time({cluster=~"tuist-$env", namespace="kura", container="kura"} | pod=~"$pod" | json [$__auto]))

spec.description: Lines per query step by `level`, parsed out of the runtime's JSON logs. A step in ERROR/WARN is the cheapest first read on whether a pod's problem is loud or silent; every level dropping to zero on a live pod means the runtime stopped logging (wedged), not that it went quiet.
spec.title: Log volume by level

spec.description: Lines per query step per pod, unparsed. With several pods selected this is where one node that is retrying or thrashing separates itself from its peers.
spec.title: Log volume by pod

spec.description: ERROR and WARN lines only. Expand a line to read the span fields the runtime stamps on every log (`span_kura_tenant_id`, `span_kura_region`, `trace_id`) and use `trace_id` to jump to the matching trace in the Traces row.
spec.title: Errors & warnings

spec.description: Every line from the selected pods, JSON-parsed. Panel controls are on so a line filter can be typed here without leaving the dashboard. Non-JSON output (panics, pre-telemetry boot lines) still shows up, flagged with a parser error rather than dropped.
spec.title: Kura logs

spec.description: Most recent spans exported by the selected pods, with liveness, readiness, scrape and rollout-status routes excluded so real client work is what's left. Traces carry the node's `kura.region`, `kura.tenant_id` and `geo.*` resource attributes, so a span identifies the node that served it.
spec.title: Recent traces

spec.query:
{ resource.service.namespace = "kura" && resource.deployment.environment.name = "$env" && resource.service.name =~ "^(${pod})$"
  && span.http.route !~ "^(/up|/ready|/metrics|/status/rollout)$"
  && duration > 500ms } with (most_recent=true)

spec.description: Requests that took longer than half a second. Read alongside `public_request_latency_seconds` in the HTTP row: the histogram says the tail exists, this says which routes and payloads are in it.
spec.title: Slow traces (> 500 ms)

spec.query:
{ resource.service.namespace = "kura" && resource.deployment.environment.name = "$env" && resource.service.name =~ "^(${pod})$"
  && (status = error || span.http.response.status_code >= 500) } with (most_recent=true)

spec.description: Spans the runtime marked as errored, plus anything that answered 5xx. Empty here while `http_exceptions_total` climbs means the failures are being turned into 4xx responses, not faults.
spec.title: Error traces

spec.description: Mesh-internal traffic only (`/_internal/*`): peer replication applies, backfill listings and body fetches. This is the row to open when the outbox or backfill panels show work that is not draining.
spec.title: Peer replication & backfill traces

spec.expr:
sum by (region) (
  sum by (pod) (rate(kura_http_requests_total_total{cluster=~"tuist-$env", pod=~"$pod", route!~"/up|/ready|/metrics|/status/rollout|/_unmatched|/_internal/.*"}[5m]))
  * on (pod) group_left(region) max by (pod, region) (kura_node_geo_info{cluster=~"tuist-$env", pod=~"$pod"})
)
or sum by (region) (max by (pod, region) (kura_node_geo_info{cluster=~"tuist-$env", pod=~"$pod"}) * 0)

SELECT __value__ AS Value, region,
  CASE region
    WHEN 'us-east'                 THEN 38.7509
    WHEN 'us-west'                 THEN 45.5229
    WHEN 'eu-central'              THEN 48.8566
    WHEN 'ca-east'                 THEN 45.3168
    WHEN 'ap-southeast'            THEN 1.3521
    WHEN 'scw-fr-par-runners'      THEN 48.7871
    WHEN 'hetzner-staging-runners' THEN 50.4779
    ELSE NULL
  END AS lat,
  CASE region
    WHEN 'us-east'                 THEN -77.6003
    WHEN 'us-west'                 THEN -122.9898
    WHEN 'eu-central'              THEN 2.3522

Coordinates are the datacentre cities behind `Tuist.Kura.Regions`; a region with no mapped coordinates is left off the map and shows up only in the table beside it.

spec.expr: max by (pod, region, tenant_id, country, subdivision) (kura_node_geo_info{cluster=~"tuist-$env", pod=~"$pod"})

spec.description: Every selected pod with the region, tenant and ISO country / subdivision it reports. This is the authoritative list: unlike the map it needs no coordinate mapping, so a newly added region shows up here the moment its first node scrapes.
spec.title: Node geography

spec.expr:
sum by (region) (
  sum by (pod) (rate(kura_http_requests_total_total{cluster=~"tuist-$env", pod=~"$pod", route!~"/up|/ready|/metrics|/status/rollout|/_unmatched|/_internal/.*"}[$__rate_interval]))
  * on (pod) group_left(region) max by (pod, region) (kura_node_geo_info{cluster=~"tuist-$env", pod=~"$pod"})
)

spec.description: Public request rate rolled up per region, joined from per-pod counters through `kura_node_geo_info` (the HTTP counters carry no region label of their own). Probes, scrapes, unmatched paths and mesh-internal routes are excluded, so this is client-facing traffic only.
spec.title: Request rate by region

spec.expr:
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (region, le) (
  sum by (pod, le) (rate(kura_public_request_latency_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"tuist-$env", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))
  * on (pod) group_left(region) max by (pod, region) (kura_node_geo_info{cluster=~"tuist-$env", pod=~"$pod"})
))

spec.description: p95 of `public_request_latency_seconds` per region. Regions serve different client populations over different paths, so a tail that belongs to one region is a routing or placement question, not a runtime one.
spec.title: p95 public latency by region

spec.expr:
sum by (region) (
  sum by (pod) (rate(kura_artifact_egress_bytes_total_total{cluster=~"tuist-$env", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))
  * on (pod) group_left(region) max by (pod, region) (kura_node_geo_info{cluster=~"tuist-$env", pod=~"$pod"})
)

spec.description: Bytes served to clients per region. Read against the region's node NIC budget (`Bare-metal capacity` on Tuist Kura) when deciding whether a region needs another box.
spec.title: Artifact egress by region

spec.description:
Replication outbox messages waiting to be processed, split by drain lane

The bulk lane (non-inline upserts, i.e. segment-backed artifacts) drains one delivery at a time, bounded by OUTBOX_MAX_INFLIGHT. The metadata lane (inline upserts and namespace deletes) is amortized by drain_metadata_batches, which carries many messages per request. A backlog sitting in the bulk lane points at the in-flight ceiling; one sitting in the metadata lane points at batching. The total in outbox_messages cannot separate them, and it is the total that the cap and the public write gate are enforced against.

Prometheus name: `kura_outbox_lane_messages` · labels: lane
spec.title: outbox_lane_messages
